Metro: Last Light Redux is an incredible game, just like its sibling this game will keep you playing.

[h1] GAMEPLAY [/h1]
    Not much has changed since the original except that theres more variety in the weapons and a few new mutated creatures. Although I do believe they wasted the mechanic of the rail car, I think it could've been used for more.

     Though, also like 2033 there is questionable AI in some parts. Although there isn't much else to say.

[h1] STORY [/h1]
     Just like 2033, the story in this game is fantastic, if not better though at first it may seem a bit fuzzy, but definately gets better as you go!  
   It has new memorible characters that you will both love, and hate. 

  The only complaint I have is that, the one section that has nudity, the way they execute it feels a bit awkward.

     The game is very cinematic with it's story telling, making a enjoyable atmospheric and immersive experience within the game itself.

[h1] AUDIO & MUSIC [/h1]
     The music and sound design in this game is phenominal. The guns, again feel real, and powerful. While the mutants horrific and scary!

[h1] GRAPHICS [/h1]
     The graphics in this game are definately better then 2033, and the lighting even moreso. The game is just beautiful to look at, especially the new surface world. Which you spend more time on thankfully to take the beauty in. 

[h1] OVERALL [/h1]
     While Last Light doesn't change much, gameplay wise from 2033, thats okay because the formula used works so well with the game, Last Light gets an [h1] 8/10 [/h1], a great game just like it's sibling!

Having played Metro: 2033 Redux I was suitably impressed by its story, graphics and gameplay, but was left wanting more. Metro: Last Light Redux offers more and I jumped straight in with an aprehensive smile on my face and a spare pair of pants by my side. So, what did I think?

I freaking LOVE this game! A brilliant continuation of the story and once again the graphics are next to none. New enemies add to the scare factor and the lore of the games' setting. Everything that made Metro: 2033 Redux so good is back but with even more. The length of the gameplay for me was longer than the first game, which was welcome.

If you enjoyed Metro: 2033 Redux (I know I did) then you should definately purchase Metro: Last Light Redux. For me it ticked ALL the boxes and still managed to scare the S**T out of me! For this one reason I praise this game so highly. Never since the likes of AvP 2000 has a game managed to quicken my pulse and caused me to pause a game to take a breath. Developers take note, this is how you make a true FPS with horror elements.

9/10

The differences  between [i]Metro 2033[/i] to [i]Metro 2033 Redux[/i] are significant while the differences between [i]Metro: Last Light[/i] and [i]Metro: Last Light Redux[/i] are unfortunately miniscule and in some cases not noticeable. I personally purchased this game for some easy achievements but that's not to say I didn't enjoy what I experienced. However, I feel there's a bit to praise and criticize 4A Games on with this product.

[h1][b][u]Note worthy additions to Metro: Last Light Redux:[/u][/b][/h1]

● Enhanced lighting. This time around Metro: Last Light has been brightened and it now features lens flares! Whether it's for the better, that's up to you to decide!

● Many textures in Metro: Last Light Redux have been slightly enhanced. However, this enhancement will not be noticeable unless you're running the graphical settings on Very High.

● Enemies are now more responsive to light and sound. If you fall from a high place or turn off a light, expect an enemy to investigate.

● The addition of safes. Hidden throughout the game are safes with corresponding keys. These safes contain a variety of items including ammunition, military grade ammunition, grenades, throwing knives, etc.

[b][u]Chapter enhancements (For users who have played through the original Metro: Last Light)[/u][/b]

[spoiler]In the chapter Reich, you now have the ability to jump when you're in the chase scene with Pavel.[/spoiler]

[spoiler]While fighting the Rhino in the chapter Undercity, nosalises will now attack you. It makes fighting the Rhino a little more challenging, but not nothing you shouldn't be able to handle.[/spoiler]


[h1][b][u]Aspects of Metro: Last Light Redux worth praising:[/u][/b][/h1]

● The ability to approach a combat situation in multiple ways. Sneaking, knock out kills, use of silencers, and using the darkness to sneak up on enemies. It may seem silly and common knowledge but many games in the current gaming industry fail to deliver anything more than just a watered down run and gun experience.

● The new A.I. combat subroutines are irritating yet innovative. If you're approaching a combat situation guns blazing be prepard for some jumpy, trigger happy enemies.

● The achievement progress saving system. In the original Metro: Last Light, progress was saved in a consecutive playthough. This time around you can reload checkpoints to accumulate kills, unlock safes, filter air time, burn cobwebs and unscrew light bulbs. 

● No unsynced voice and facial animations. Although a little wonky, the facial animations and voice are never unsynced from start to finish. That's certainly saying something considering the majority of the games created today have the issue with unsynced facial animations.

● No in-game store. The majority of developers feel the need to put a direct link to their game's downloadable content within the game itself. This angers some consumers while ruining the immersion they're trying to create.


[h1][b][u]Aspects of Metro: Last Light Redux worth criticizing:[/u][/b][/h1]

● Non-existant NPC eye tracking. I never realized how important eye tracking was before I played the Metro series. Almost all of the NPCs in Metro: Last Light Redux feel as if they're staring off into space, unaware of their surroundings or the player.

● Copy and paste menus and user interface. The menu and user interface of Metro: Last Light Redux is the exact menu and user interface that Metro: Last Light used back in 2013.

● The watering down of achievements within the game. While they may have added 5 new achievements, they have completely gutted 28 from the game, including ones that were from once downloadable content.

I love how much goes on around you, even when your in a different room you can hear conversations between NPCs. Sometimes I just take 5 minutes out of my session to just vibe and listen to what's going on. They did a good job of giving npcs lives to live.

Metro: Last Light is pretty cool, I guess. 

You play as Artyom, a man who lives in the Moscow Metro because some jerks with big red buttons decided to push the big red buttons and kill us all. 

During World War 3 in 2013, a war I apparently missed, it all got too hot and everyone decided to nuke everyone. Major cities across the world were burned away in nuclear hellfire and most of the human race was wiped out. Fortunately, 200,000 residents of Moscow managed to avoid being turned into the skeletons form Terminator 2 by hiding underground in the Moscow Metro station. 
It is now 2034, and the Metro has taken on a society of it's own. Less than 50,000 people of the original 200,000 are alive in these Metro tunnels, but they have formed their own brand of society and go about their day to day lives working, exploring, farming, and of course, waging war.

Because what screams post-apocalyptic Metro tunnels more than Nazis fighting Communists? 

Metro: Last Light is a first person shooter where you, playing as Artyom, must travel through the Moscow Metro in search for the last Dark One, a survivor of a race of strange creatures that were wiped out in the last game.  But after being captured, Artyom is cut off from his faction, the Rangers of the Order, and has to travel through a hostile Metro while fighting Nazis, bandits, mutants, your mother, and several other enemies that want you dead. 

Metro: Fast Food puts a big emphasis on resource management, ammo and supplies CAN be scarce within the metro tunnels if you're a big stinky man who doesn't know how to manage his things properly. Artyom is a very sneaky fellow, and usually has the advantage of not being seen when he goes into a new area. As long as you stay out of sight and avoid light sources, the enemy shouldn't be able to see you, allowing you to plan out your attacks and pick off stragglers and loners as you see fit. Or you can just avoid them all together and stock everything like the hermit you are. 

The game gives you a lot of options for handling enemies and dangerous situations. Not only are all of the weapons weighty and crunchy to fire, but you also have a knife that lets you dispatch enemies quietly as well as throwing knives for when you want to do your best ninja impression. Not only that but you can carry three firearms at any given time and customize them to meet most situations. A silencer for when you want to be sneaky, IR scopes so you can see in the dark better, and even a suppressor for your shotgun because 'No Country For old Men' was a rad movie. 

You also have two types of ammunition, or at least two types of ammo for weapons that can fire Soviet 5.45x39mm cartridges. See, I did my research.
These "golden bullets" have become a currency in the Metro tunnel. The way it's explained is that the bullets aren't backed by any kind of currency standard like the NCR money was in Fallout, but instead they're prized for their stopping power and penetration. So you have a choice to make, hold on to these bullets and spend them as currency, or use them in your gun if for any reason you feel as though the shoddy and poorly made dirty rounds that are manufactured in the metro just wont cut it. 

The game is linear, but honestly, what do you expect when you're walking through a literal metro tunnel. The game does open up and allow you a bit of freedom when you enter stations with enemy encounters. But for the most part, you're on the rails, no pun intended. It's not a bad way for the game, considering how narrative heavy it actually is, and I never really felt all that oppressed when going through it, there's still enough room to scavenge and hunt for supplies in between sneaking and fire fights, which is more than you can say for most linear games. 

But should you play Metro: cockfight? 

The game's linearity may ward you off, and the mutant fights feel like nothing more than events that happen only to drain your resources. The boss fights are fairly boring, but they only happen twice or so throughout the entire game.

I would say Metro works as a nice gateway for people into the Eastern European Post Apocalyptic genre. It shares many similarities with another series of the same genre known as STALKER, who both borrow heavily from  Arkady and Boris Strugatsky 1971 classic novel: Roadside Picnic. It's a very different take on the genre than you might be use to. There's this overlying feeling of...I don't know, hope I guess. There are crazies and freaks in the Metro, but it's not like raiders and bandits completely outnumber and overwhelm the decent folk like the modern Fallout games, and it's not like Mad Max where everyone is living off borrowed time and outside of things like ghosts and mutants, it feels more grounded in reality.

The people aren't living off borrowed time, they picked up where they left off and struggle to make with what they can. Don't get me wrong, living in the Metro tunnels would still be a terrible and dreadful experience, but if you held on, if you struggled and fought with everyone else, you can make a life for yourself in those dark, old tunnels. And even though you might never see it, maybe, just maybe, your children, or your children's children can stand on the surface world without radiation suits and gas masks, and can build a new world from the ruins of the old one. Maybe there is a light at the end of that tunnel...

[h1]Another masterpiece[/h1]

Sometimes it happens that a sequel to a successfull game is bad. Metro: Last Light is not one of them, it's another high quality post-apocalyptic game with excellent atmosphere.

The story is set 1 year after Metro 2033. If you are reading this review as a someone who never played any Metro games (or read books of well known Russian writer Dmitry Glukhovsky) , you are probably wondering if you need to play 2033 before Last Light to understand the story - the answer is [b]yes[/b]. Last Light is a direct sequel with many references to 2033's story. There is no explanation what happened in D6 and why everybody wants it. I recommend playing 2033 before Last Light, it's a great game and it's easy to buy both on sale in the Metro bundle.

The whole metro is preparing for war after D6 was found by Artyom and his companions. Not only that, [spoiler]one of the dark ones survived[/spoiler] and it's up to Artyom to find him because he was the only one connected to them. I don't want to spoil the story so I will stop here.

The gameplay is exactly the same like Metro 2033 - a linear first person shooter without any cut scenes, Artyom doesn't speak (although I think he should start speaking because it's... just weird sometimes) and the player has to follow a determined path. It's basically Half-Life style gameplay. I'm glad that the level design is not chaotic like in 2033 where I was sometimes running out of ideas where am I supposed to go and had to watch YT videos. It's less scary than 2033 which was sometimes almost a survival horror but the asmosphere is still great, even depressing in some moments [spoiler]like the plane crash scene[/spoiler].
Graphics looks great, it's very close to Metro 2033 Redux. Again, beautiful combination of lights, particle effects, shadows and detailed level design.

I recommend playing with Russian dubbing because the whole game is in Russia. It's weird to see Russians speaking English. You can always turn on English subtitles and trust me - the atmosphere and overall experience is much better with Russian dubbing.

[h1]Linux[/h1]
I was very happy with the quality of Metro 2033 Linux version and I can say the same about Last Light - no issues, no fps drops, runs great. For some reason Metro games don't feel like direct Windows to Linux ports but somehow separately crafted for Linux. It even runs faster on Linux (with SSAA off) than Windows according to all benchmarks on YouTube.

[h1]Summary[/h1]
If you never played Metro, get 2033 first. If you find it enjoyable, get Last Light and you won't be dissapointed.

Metro: Last Light Redux — Achievement Hunter Review

🕒 Time played: 26 hours
🏆 Completion: 100% game completion + all Steam achievements

As an achievement hunter, I completed Metro: Last Light Redux in 26 hours, unlocking every Steam achievement and finishing all of the DLC content.

I already have experience with the Metro series, so I'd like to give some advice to anyone planning to go for 100% completion.

The game essentially requires two different playthrough styles:

Stealth Playthrough – where you try not to kill anyone and instead knock enemies out whenever possible.
Spartan Playthrough – where you can go all out, kill everything in your path, and focus purely on completing the story.

My stealth run took around 14–15 hours because I was collecting everything and making sure not to miss any achievements. The Spartan run, on the other hand, only took about 5–6 hours since all the collectibles and miscellaneous achievements had already been completed during the first playthrough. At that point, I could simply run through the levels and eliminate anyone who got in my way.

The remaining time was spent completing the DLCs, where you get to play as several other characters from the Metro universe, including Pavel, Khan, and others. I actually enjoyed these additional stories because they added more background to the world and its characters.

There was one achievement that required collecting artifacts and selling them at the base. Fortunately, there are plenty of Steam guides and YouTube videos that show efficient routes and methods for unlocking it quickly, so I wouldn't worry too much about that one.

As for the game itself, I really enjoyed it. The story is engaging, the atmosphere is excellent, the graphics still look great, and the gameplay remains fun throughout the entire experience.

From an achievement hunter's perspective, this game didn't feel particularly difficult. It doesn't require an extreme amount of time, skill, or grinding compared to many other games I've completed.

Great story and atmosphere
Excellent graphics
Fun gameplay and gunplay
Interesting DLC content
Fair and manageable achievement list
Two playthroughs feel different enough to stay enjoyable

❌ Cons:

Requires multiple playthroughs for 100%
Some collectible cleanup may be needed

[b]Artyom's journey continues[/b]

When it comes to continuing Artyom's story the creators decided to consider the bad ending of the first Metro game. Artyom, now residing at D6, is visited by Khan who tells him that apparently a Dark One survived and their task is now to capture it. Things, of course, do not go as planned and you'll soon be imprisoned by the Reich. We meet Pavel and for some time we travel together following our successful escape. Once again we have a main mission visible on Artyom's notebook but it always has additional tasks depending on which level we are. There are 30 chapters - the story has a decent longevity offering at least 10 hours of playtime.

[b]New features[/b]

Well, it's difficult to review Last Light now that the prequel is only available in the Redux version. It was Last light introducing melee executions with a knife including the ability to knock out our enemies. The latter is important for the good ending - once again the game employs a moral system which determines the two possible endings. It was also Last Light where light bulbs could be removed instead of having to shoot them. Stealth became better in the sequel and some new enemy types were introduced such as the shrimps. Especially the bigger versions are annoying. Also, Last Light features a couple of boss battles just to make the gameplay even more challenging. In any case, most of the new stuff were reintroduced in Metro 2033 when its Redux edition was released.

[b]Going Redux with Last Light[/b]

What if you already have the vanilla version? What more can Redux give you? Unfortunately, not much. Don't expect a major overhaul like the one they did with Metro 2033. The name here is completely misleading - the Redux version comes with all DLC contents pre-installed; no more, no less. They could have just called it the Definitive or Ultimate Edition. There are some videos out there showcasing the graphics differences between the original and the Redux version but I'm simply unable to take note of any difference. Some of the lighting may have improved but not significantly. 

You'll also notice that we now only have 49 achievements. This means that decreasing the number makes it easier to reach 100% completion. Some of the more difficult achievements such as completing the game in Ranger Hardcore are now absent. You'll still have the good ending you have to do and the extremely challenging Tower Pack, mind you!

[b]Summarium[/b]

If you already have Last Light there's no point in purchasing the Redux version as it simply is a newer edition released with all its contents but with fewer 'cheevos. If you are a Metro fan like myself who is annoyed by the removal of Exodus from the store page but adult enough not to go ranting about it by downvoting the prequels you can buy it for old times' sake.

[h1]INTRODUCTION:[/h1]
Metro Last Light Redux is the ‘remastered’ version of Metro Last Light which was originally released in 2013. The game is a linear first-person horror survival shooter which was generally based on the novels (Metro 2033 and Metro 2034) written by Dmitry Glukhovsky. This game serves as the sequel to the critically acclaimed 2010 game, Metro 2033.

[h1]PLOT (No Spoilers):[/h1]
One year after the events of Metro 2033, Artyom (Артём) finds himself as a full-fledged member of the [i]Spartans[/i] who has set up shop in the massive Soviet bunker known as D6. After receiving word that a Dark One survived the ‘canonical ending’ of Metro 2033, Artyom sets out on another adventure in the post-apocalyptic world to capture this last surviving Dark One.

[h1]PROS:[/h1]
+ Excellent graphics
+ Excellent atmosphere (blend of action, horror, suspense and mystery)
+ Excellent world building
+ Very good sound design
+ Very good map and level design
+ Very good story which is told in a fairly lengthy game time
+ Subtle morality system that will have an effect on the final outcome of the story
+ New game mechanics (ex. Stealth takedowns – lethal or non-lethal)
+ Very fun gunplay
+ Improved enemy AI
+ Improved character animations from the first game
+ Extensive weapon selection and upgrade system
+ Fair but challenging difficulty
+ Very fun and relatively challenging DLCs
+ Lap dances

[h1]CONS:[/h1]
- No Field of View (FOV) slider: Note that the default setting is 50.625, which is too narrow (in my opinion) for a first-person shooter game. [b][url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=965573251&searchtext=FOV]FIX[/url][/b]
- Rare crashing issues
- Ridiculously (unskippable) long intro cinematics [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/43160/discussions/0/846960628361921807/]FIX[/url][/b] [i]<-I have personally not tried this[/i]
- Although there are improvements in the overall animations of the characters, facial animations can still use a little bit more polishing.

[h1]NEUTRAL:[/h1]
+/- All weapon mods/upgrades can only be removed if you visit the weapon shops. This means that you cannot remove your silencer at will.
+/- Armor upgrades are now tied to the story and can no longer be purchased, unlike the first original game.
+/- Cliché boss battles

[h1]CONCLUSION:[/h1]
[b]GREAT GAME[/b] and [b]GREAT SEQUEL[/b]. Metro Last Light Redux is a worthy successor to Metro 2033. Much like the original game, it delivers a unique and very immersive first-person shooter experience while bringing in several game mechanics that add to the atmosphere and immersion of the game. It blends together the atmosphere of narrative driven games, the suspense of horror games, and the heart pumping combat of action games.

[h1]WORTH IT?[/h1]
The game is worth $19.99 (or your regional equivalent). If you’re new to the Metro series, I would personally recommend that you purchase the [b][url=http://store.steampowered.com/sub/44169/]Metro Redux Bundle[/url][/b] because its only $29.98. If that’s still too expensive, then I suggest waiting for a sale.

[h1]FINAL NOTES:[/h1]
This is not an open world Action-RPG game like S.T.A.L.K.E.R or Fallout. The Metro series falls in line with games such as F.E.A.R., DOOM, and Half-Life which are narrative driven games.

Note that the original Metro Last Light (2013) game is no longer available on Steam. As of the time of this review, it has been replaced by the Redux version.

      I heard about the [i]Metro[/i] series for a while now but never had the chance to play them until I finally picked them up off a [i]Steam[/i] sale. There were many aspects I liked about the game as soon as I jumped in. Personally, I find that when you play a single player, first person shooter game, it can go one of two ways. Firstly it can either be a good mix of an action/first person shooter/and or adventure game, keeping one drawn in with various tasks, different sceneries, and things to do besides move and shoot. However, first person shooter games could just be that. With no real motivation to do any specific tasks you could quickly find yourself noticing all you do is move and shoot. I can tell you with ease that this isn't the case with [i]Metro: Last Light Redux[/i]. I liked that the game kept it from feeling like most bad first person shooter games and instead followed my first description; various tasks, different scenarios and things to do. I also liked how the story had multiple endings, it added replayability to the game. Especially because you have to work through a single play through to get to one or the other of the endings. Possibly making your second play through different then your first. Amongst other things, I also really liked the weapon customization. It's always a better experience when you play a game and get to make things your own, i.e. naming characters, making decisions and or customizing things.

      To be honest, there isn't a whole lot I don't like about this game. While usually I try to make sure I throw some points in for the other side of the argument, I honestly can't think of some genuine things that you could dislike about the game. [b]PERSONALLY[/b] I don't like the outside segments and really the only reason for this is because of how perceptive you need to be [u](unless using a guide)[/u]. What I mean by this is that the outside can be overwhelming your first time through. It'll seem like there's so much to explore and it'll seem like it'll be easy to miss something. Which it is. However, I don't feel as though this is a flaw in the gameplay and don't see this as a argument to be made not to buy the game.

     Would I recommend this game? Yes! I feel as though it's one of the better (if not best) first person shooter games I've played in a long time. I like the stealth mixed into the gameplay. Personally, I'm always a huge fan of stealth so that was a big thing for me. I liked the weapon customization along with the story. The moral choices and the alternate endings are a plus as well as it adds on replayability. 

     [b][u][i]NOTE:[/i][/u][/b] The game does have nudity in two levels that you can't skip by and can't select an option for it not to be. As much as I don't have a problem with this, I feel as though it should be included in this review!

Metro: Last Light Redux is a post-apocalyptic story-rich first person shooter developed by 4A Games and published by Deep Silver. Spartan ranger Artyom returns once again this time on the trail of the last Dark One left alive following the events of the previous title Metro: 2033 Redux. In doing so, he haphazardly stumbles upon a plot by the Communist Reds to take the newly acquired D6 facility from the Spartans and wage war throughout the Metro to gain control of everything and everyone within it. Step into Artyom's boots and take yet another highly interactive adventure through both the dark dangerous tunnels of the terrifying Moscow Metro and the horribly irradiated surface of the world above.

[h1]GAMEPLAY[/h1]

First and foremost this is one of the most interactive first person shooters available. That is a "tagline" that I'd been hearing about these games for years but I actually had to learn about this the hard way...by playing this fantastic title. Artyom interacts with the environment in a number of ways by doing things that we do in everyday life all the time and take for granted but it's these little things like opening doors, flipping switches, eating, drinking, pulling ourselves up a ledge that make the connection between the in-game character and the player that much more intense and immersive. Ha ha! When WAS the last time that you actually pulled yourself up a ledge? Well you get what I'm implying so that's what actually matters yes?! 

As with most F.P.S. titles the gunplay is fast, frenetic and highly enjoyable. The large variety of weapons that were available in Metro 2033 Redux are also for use in Metro: Last Light Redux with the introduction of a few new guns such as the Valve which is a sniper rifle and definitely one of my favorites of the bunch. With the wide selection available I have no doubt that you will find something that fits your style of play whether it be guns blazing or stealth. Moving on, this titles missions for the most part are just as non-linear as the previous game in that you can often choose different routes and methods in order to complete your tasks. As someone who highly enjoys stealth games I really enjoyed this option in the gameplay. Wrap all that around a thrilling story that keeps you on the edge of your seat as it progresses and this makes for a wonderfully developed gaming experience.

[h1]VISUALS[/h1] 

Once again 4A Games creates another masterpiece in the revisioning of this wonderfully immersive title. I never played the original versions of the games which is a shame as I would like to have tried them as well so I could compare the differences between them and the redux versions myself. Nevertheless, Metro: Last Light Redux is a beautiful game with fantastic textures, lighting and exceptional animation on the extremely life-like and very believable characters in the story. Often times whenever I made it to a new station I would find myself wandering around observing the highly detailed surroundings and people as well as listening in on the many conversations taking place around me as the citizens go about their daily routines. Heavy praise for the developers as the game does a fantastic job of making you feel as though you are in a living breathing world, as decimated as it might be, but a world full of life nonetheless. 

[h1]CONCLUSION[/h1]

This title was a fascinating continuation of the Metro franchise and gave me an even deeper understanding into the lore of the games which have quickly become one of my favorite series in the very popular post-apocalyptic genre. The story was highly enjoyable and the combat alot of fun. On a side note, I didn't have many technical issues with the title other than the game crashing on me once and twice I ran into some unresponsive N.P.C.'s which forced me to exit out and reload a save. As with the previous title Metro 2033 Redux I really enjoyed the playthrough and this was also a great transition to the next game in the franchise Metro Exodus. Option-wise, there are many Steam Achievements to hunt down and Steam Trading Cards to collect as well. In conclusion, this title excelled at broadening Artyom's story with even more immersive gameplay and lore than before so Metro: Last Light Redux is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED to first person shooter, post-apocalyptic, story-rich gamers one and all!

Last Light is at its core an action-horror game. A genre that can never quite seem to find a perfect harmony between the two very different elements involved.
Moscow is beautifully depressing in its decayed state, but behind that beauty lies an even greater threat than the metro can offer. Radiation. Radiation is a constant threat on the surface and you will need to continually find filters for your gasmask to cleanse the contaminated air. Should you run out of filters, your screen will slowly turn red as you suffocate and die. This mixed with the mutated creatures, which inhabit Moscow, continually hunting you as you make your way towards your destination makes for some tense situations. Imagine you forgot to change your air-filter and you hear the beeping noise that indicates your about to run out of oxygen , then the moment you start to replace your filter is the exact moment that a pack of irradiated mutants decide they want a snack and your face is the best option. What do you do? Do you replace the filter while they attack and hope you'll still have enough time to fight back before one of them tears your throat out, or do you stop changing the filter so you can pull out your gun and kill the creatures before you suffocate? These split-second decisions are what keeps the combat interesting throughout the whole experience.
With the metro and Moscow being such fascinating places to explore, it's unfortunate that a lot of the game is extremely guided. 
Last Light manages to overcome its flaws through a sheer abundance of personality. After a slow start it quickly finds its rhythm and manages to stay on beat, achieving an almost masterful execution of pacing throughout the rest of your quest to save the metro and the future of humanity. Metro: Last Light is also one of the most thematically cohesive games I have ever played. From the gameplay to the sound design to the art direction and visuals it's all a cacophony of dreadfulness that will keep you gripping the controller tightly in your hands(or hugging the keyboard to your chest like a newborn baby) until the credits roll.

[h1]Overview[/h1]
[b]Metro Last Light Redux[/b] is a post-apocalyptic FPS, direct sequel to [i]Metro 2033[/i], and still developed by [i]4A Games[/i]. In this game [b]set after the "canon" ending of 2033[/b] (the destruction of a certain enemy), players will still [b]impersonate Artyom, now promoted to full-fledged Spartan Ranger[/b] due to his extraordinary exploits, and sent to a new mission that could potentially decide the future of the whole metro, under a new insidious threat. 

[b]This sequel improves almost all aspects that already made 2033 a masterpiece[/b]: weapon and consumable variety has improved significantly, offering players a wider selection throughout the adventure. [b]The Karma system is now more in-depth[/b], as performing "good" (such as avoiding certain fights, helping people, or for some weird reason listening to the end to random dialogues) or "evil" (such as killing enemies who already surrendered, or ignoring a call for help) actions will [b]influence the ending significantly, the number of such interactions is much greater[/b]. 

The [b]stealth system has been somewhat improved[/b] with enemies reacting more realistically and also a lot more sections where a stealth approach is viable, if not strongly suggested, but by no means mandatory. [b]The presence of many included Extra Missions, where players will impersonate different characters[/b] such as Khan or enemy factions members, [b]is surely interesting[/b] despite them being of inconsistent quality and some being more of a pain than anything else. 

Overall [b]Metro Last Light Redux[/b] is an incredible game, improving the already excellent formula of its prequel to new heights, while delivering the same feel, gameplay mechanics and wonderful art direction that made 2033 a success. [b]Offering a campaign 9-12 hours long depending a lot on approach, exploration and time spent listening to dialogues, while a couple more hours (3-4) for completing all the Extra Missions, for a base price of 20€ I can absolutely recommend getting this full price without a second thought.[/b]

[h1]In-Depth Breakdown[/h1]

🎮 [b]Gameplay Analysis[/b]
The gameplay of Metro Last Light is divided into Exploration, Character Management, and Combat.

[b]Exploration[/b] in actually the main activity in Metro, more so than combat: crossing the frozen wastes of the surface, or the dark tunnels underground, players will find themselves going through a variety of environments mostly on foot, where a keen eye for secondary areas and loot are essential. With superb environments and graphics, exploring every new area is an experience best taken slowly, not only to find most secrets and loot which is important, but also to savor the atmosphere. While on "regular" difficulties HUD and some hints will help you finding loot, where to go more easily, the Ranger difficulty, which delivers the "true" Metro experience, removed HUD completely, delivering a realism level very few games dare having. Safes unlocked with keys found in other places, rooms, sometimes whole buildings can be areas off the beaten path, containing not just supplies but even scorches of lore to expend your knowledge.

[b]Character Management[/b] is all about resource conservation: with limits to every type of bullets, consumables and medkits you can carry, making every shot count, healing when really necessary and making a run for it when needs be are all things to take into account, as said before, looting every possible resource is fundamental. In peaceful stations, players can sell unused bullets for military grade ammo which doubles as currency, in order to buy new weapons, modify existing ones, or replenish supplies - everything comes at high prices though, only the most conservative players will be able to afford the priciest weapons and modifications before late-game. In contaminated areas, keeping an eye on remaining filters for your mask, and its integrity, are also added mechanics to keep up pressure.

[b]Combat[/b] is perhaps the best aspect of Metro, delivering an uncompromising, realistic system where a few shots can kill both yourself and most enemies. Ammo is generally scarce, grenades and high caliber guns instantly kill pretty much always, while the enemy at least on Ranger Hardcore, employs good tactics, uses cover and generally puts up a good fight also for superior numbers. Stealth or loud, which are both completely viable at all difficulties, Metro's combat delivers excellent gun feeling, realism, and brutality, as it should be.

You know when you read a book/movie/tv/game series and you get to the end and just want more? I'm replaying this for the third time and I still get that craving for more once I've finished. It's a very well made game for one, having many different mechanics at work often all at the same time.
You'll need to manage your air supply when in toxic environments, represented as your gas mask filters which you will need to swap out every 5 minutes. You'll need to make sure your torch is topped up with energy, manually pumping the thing every now and again and you'll also need to make sure you're hidden from view, highlighted by the blue vial on your watch. 

*This game requires a moderatly well equipped computer to run at reasonable framerates.* The framerate itself is fairly stable and doesn't stutter or dip, at least that I know of.

Explore the tunnels of the metro, the horrors of the destroyed Moscow city as you climb through the ruins of the city, dodging the shadows that flash every time lightning strikes. You'll then realise the shadows look noticeably human like. Enjoy the flashbacks to the last moments of the Russians' lives as they react to the explosion in the distance. You'll see many things in this game, you'll experience many different fear invoking reactions. If you hate spiders, you'll be scared. If you cannot stand small spaces, you'll be breathing hard. If the thought of the supernatural sends shivers down your spine you might consider putting on a jumper because being cold will be the new norm for you.
This game should be played after you finish Metro 2033 (redux preferred) as playing this first will really not make any sense at all. 

If you choose to play this game, you'll be choosing to experience a fantastic storyline, spread over the two games and several DLC levels alongside the amazingly well polished gameplay that comes from managing your gas mask filters, gas mask screen (It cracks, you start dying) and the dirt and blood that comes from shooting dirty/bloody objects, or being shot yourself. I would give this game a 8/10 if not a 9/10.
The only reason I cannot give this game a 10/10 is because I personally find the ghost sections to be too uncomfortable for me to handle. And although I mention spiders being prominent I should mention one of the DLC's is literally just you being given a flamethrower and you burning down a spider nest. That was very enjoyable. Otherwise this game is flawless in my opinion and I'd recommend it to anyone, even those scared of the mentioned things because it's truly an experience that cannot be beaten.

I cannot measure this game in the finite terms of numbers, this is a masterpiece, far beyond any rating, exceptionally charged and absolutely raw. This experience will live long into my future, and no suprise I would let my own son and daughter experience it in 20 years time.

This is a thing of pure art, it should be preserved in the great library of human thought and development, preserved for generations to experience, through a heartfelt, honest but raw and untouched story that if we do not work together, arms linked against the wind, then what are we, men against a blaze of progress that we cannot control? I have said more than enough, experience this, you have not understood true passion and pain until you venture into the Metro.

[h2]TLDR:[/h2] A decent follow-up to the first game, with a handful of persistent problems.

[h2]GAMEPLAY OVERVIEW:[/h2] Metro: Last Light Redux is the second game in the series, picking up after Metro 2033. Based on the Metro novels, the games center around a young man named Artyom, who is a resident of the maze-like Moscow subways after a nuclear war devastated the surface.

Last Light takes place a year after the first game, during which the dark ones—sinister supernatural figures—were thought to have been wiped out. Artyom becomes aware of a surviving dark one, is taken on a mission to destroy it, and gets embroiled in a new web of evil plots that threaten the survival of everyone in the metro.

Last Light features two main gameplay modes: Survival and Spartan, the former offering less ammo, supplies, and durability for player and foe alike, and the latter making the game more of a shooter, with abundant supplies and the player being able to take more punishment. With each of those play styles, there are also difficulties, the hardest of which turns off crosshairs and interaction markers. Gameplay is in first-person throughout and the player's character never speaks, save when narrating between chapters.

Artyom can carry up to three weapons (two on the hardest difficulty), appropriate ammunition, explosives, and med kits. Aside from weapons, the player will need to manage their light source, which can be revitalized by a handheld charger, and in toxic areas or the radioactive surface, their gas mask canisters. Some settlements offer shops for weapons and supplies, and as before, the currency of the subways is pre-war military rounds (valued for their better quality and rarity). Pre-war rounds can also be used in some weapons. They hit harder than standard ammo but the player is literally firing away money, so it's a tradeoff.

Threats come hard and fast, both from humans and various mutated monsters. Combat can be difficult and unforgiving, especially against multiple foes. In most situations against human enemies, the player will have the choice of sneaking past, or at least taking some opponents out via stealth methods (lethal or non), which can make those confrontations much easier. The player usually has options in these situations, and can approach the scenario with guns blazing, in complete stealth, or anything in between. Some monster fights can be avoided but these are less common.

Last Light also sports a handful of unavoidable set pieces against boss mobs that can't be stealthed past. In theory, the boss mobs have weak spots that speed up a fight, if the player can hit them. Some are easier than others, but none are simple, and all three come with regular mobs that have to be avoided or dealt with. I found these encounters annoying, since the game's mechanics just aren't built for fast evasion, rapid dodges, or circle-strafing, so if one has trouble hitting the vulnerable spots or doesn't have a handful of powerful mines, these encounters can go south really fast. On top of that, there are some mandatory firefights against large groups of humans that are really tough. All of these bouts feel very out of place with the otherwise slow-and-steady stealthy nature of the game.

Much like its predecessor, Last Light features a "moral" system that dictates how the game ends. The player builds moral points as might be expected, by sparing enemies, avoiding unnecessary killing (of people), not stealing, aiding beggars, listening to conversations, and the like. With enough moral points, Artyom gets the "good" ending, which is the canon ending and leads to the next game. I finished the main game, with some side exploration, in about 12 hours, which seems to be about normal.

[h2]STORY / WORLDBUILDING:[/h2] The world of Last Light is grim and unforgiving, continuing the themes of the first, though to a lesser extent. MLL feels a bit less hopeless, especially within the more expansive settlement, where life seems to be slightly improved. The Spartan Rangers seem to have more control and influence as they protect the people. The general background ambience, as one listens to the conversations of the background characters, comes off as much less pessimistic than the first game. 

Away from the settlements, the mood remains bleak. Some tunnels are barely passable and choked with mutants. Above ground, hideous beasts make neither land nor water safe. The supernatural factors from the first game are present once again, with the surviving dark one being a primary plot device. Artyom witnesses impressions and visions of victims of the war, as if such memories were etched into the locations. It's still a very dark game, featuring slavery, torture of prisoners, and, uh, “intimate” assault. The game most assuredly earns its Mature rating. 

The basic story revolves around several factions vying for the weaponry in the pre-war military bunker D6, discovered in the previous game. The plot is basically sound but didn't hook me as much as the first one. Several characters return from the previous game but aside from one interesting dude—who is a sometime-companion, sometime-foe—none of them get any dimension or real characterization. A female companion gets scant screen time and then is suddenly in love with Artyom. As a whole, the narrative just wasn't as cohesive as the first game.

Level design is again very linear, with numerous side paths that sometimes offer supplies or side objectives. The straightforward design works for the narrative, and the levels felt intuitive and natural, without the player feeling like they’re being channeled or in a “hallway.”

[h2]DLC:[/h2] This Redux version of Last Light comes with eight additional missions that take place around the main story, or from the perspective of other characters. I tried a few and they were okay, though I think they'll appeal most to people already digging the mechanics and ambiance of the main game.

[h2]TECHNICAL ASPECTS:[/h2] Last Light runs well for the most part, though I did have repeated bugs on loading, such as enemies who were frozen in place and unable to be killed but could still damage me or sound alarms. During a boss fight, I got stuck under its feet, was thrashed around, and clipped through the ground as it attacked. I had to reload one DLC mission twice to get a specific mission objective to activate. The bugs aren't always present but happened enough to be irritating.

Topping out Steam achievements will require at least two full runs, completing several collection objectives (such as picking up all 43 diaries), and finishing all DLC missions. Fortunately, chapter replay and easy checkpoint reloading allows completion of several of these (such as opening the same safe over and over to get the "open ten safes" achievement).

[h2]FINAL WORD:[/h2] I had a decent time with Metro Last Light. Annoyances aside, the core gameplay is good enough and the story does a good job following the first game.

Metro: Last Light Redux is a masterclass in atmospheric, post-apocalyptic storytelling. Building on the incredible foundation of its predecessor, the game plunges you back into the hauntingly beautiful, radiation-blasted ruins of the Moscow metro system.

The Redux edition includes all previously released DLC and adds new gameplay modes, letting you choose between a tense, survival-horror experience or a more action-focused shooter. Exceptional lighting, sound design, and environmental details make every encounter with the mutated deep-dwelling horrors genuinely thrilling. For newcomers to the series, this is the definitive way to experience Artyom's journey.

Key Highlights

* Immersive Atmosphere: The game perfectly captures the dread and claustrophobia of the underground tunnels, contrasted with the lethal beauty of the irradiated surface.

* Play Your Way: With the addition of "Survival" and "Spartan" modes, you can choose between a scarce, methodical survival experience or a more combat-heavy, resource-rich approach.

* The Definitive Package: It includes all the original DLC, adding hours of extra content and different perspectives on the Metro universe.

A new, even better, polished and modified part of an already cool game - non-standard and unlike other FPS Metro 2033. Once again, when our Ukrainian developers created a masterpiece, showing the “thick-walled” Western corporations what is born when a good book, talent, enthusiasm and fanaticism merge into one.

All things considered, Last Light is more than ideal for a sequel to 2033. It brings everything 2033 did to the table once again as well as its new ideas to add to Metro's world. While I don't think it hits the same peaks some moments in 2033 did, I found Last Light to overall be a more consistently improved experience.

Since the Redux Metros share the same game play, most of the positives return from 2033. Guns still feel unique and good to use, Ranger mode continues to emphasise Metro's survivalist identity (and does a much better job explaining the games mechanics this  time) and exploring the decrepit remains of Moscow remains thrilling. Unfortunately, the same problems also return. The game continues to shower you in resources & the enemy AI is kind of a joke, resulting in mostly combat that failed to engage me, at least against human enemies.

The exploration especially deserves a shout out, It would've been fine, (albeit a little bit tiring), if Last Light had shared the same snowy ruins of 2033 that invoked feelings of a dead world. Instead, we are introduced to a whole new side of Metro we haven't seen before, traversing new tunnels on the brink of collapse and a swamp-like surface, teeming with new creatures. The world felt much more alive yet hostile this time, a different feeling that worked just as well as 2033's isolated environments.

The level design in this game also feels very tightened up compared to its predecessor. There are no more outright bad levels this time, every chapter I played through was enjoyable, and after the first couple hours, the game switched up its areas just enough that it remained exciting for the remainder of its run-time. Levels in Last Light also gave the player much more freedom, You're no longer locked behind NPC's to progress the story, they serve more as assistants this time. Likewise, there were more secrets to find in each area, at least from my experience. While levels were more consistently good this time, there was only one time I was really amazed in Last Light: [spoiler] Travelling with the baby Dark One was excellent. Growing closer with the Dark One through both game play and story, while being forced to survive outside for such an extended period of time resulted in a really solid experience all around. [/spoiler] Unfortunately there aren't as many peaks as 2033 had to offer, but I'm alright with that in exchange for effectively eliminating the many level design problems 2033 had.

I'd say the only place Last Light has gotten worse is in the story department, they aren't directly adapting a book this time and it really shows. Too much of the story lacks clear direction, you spend the first half of this game gunning through levels without much reason or interest as to why. Even later on, when the story starts getting into motion, its just not very interesting, and I can think of a few reasons why. Last Light relies much more on the villains of the Metro than 2033 did, which is a shame because they're not very interesting, just generic bad guys really. There's also some really bad exposition and character interactions [spoiler] (Anna's "romance" is nothing short of terrible) [/spoiler] which really drag the story down at key points. Worst of all, there just comes a point where you seem to repeating 2033's story line, which is a shame because we end up treading through the same ideas in a less interesting way. 

It is notable however, how good the specific character writing has become. There's been a huge upgrade in both performance and script to make the denizens of the Metro feel much more alive. Kahn returns and immediately feels much more interesting than in 2033, and I feel confident in saying Pavel's jovial attitude resulted in the best character the franchise has to offer. While the main story overall lead me through an uninteresting plight, the characters that brought me through it kept me entertained.

[h1] 6/10 [/h1]

Last Light is a great improvement on 2033 in both design and mechanics. It introduces it's own identity through its world and eliminates the major flaws of 2033. It's just a shame to me that there are both enough problems returning from the previous entry and introduced in this one to stop it from being great. I'd recommend this game by itself, but I think it's best enjoyed after playing 2033 first, they fit together to make a pretty good experience.

[h1]Metro: Last Light[/h1]

[h1]"Last Bullet. Last Breath. Last Chance."[/h1]

[h1]Note:[/h1] Just like with my Metro 2033 review, this too isn't a review for Metro: Last Light Redux, this is just a review for Metro: Last Light overall, seeing as the original Metro: Last Light is no longer available on Steam with good reasons.
_____________

[h1]Introduction:[/h1]
The sequel to my favorite game of all time. I still remember the day when the teaser trailer was revealed. It was this exact [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W1omOscHnSM]one here[/url] and even though an average gamer wouldn't understand much from this. I did. I learned a lot of new things just by watching this and this trailer had raised my hype level like no other one before. The second place that year went to Borderlands 2 which was announced just a couple of months later. I felt like my entire life had a new meaning. I felt the hype levels flowing through my blood cells. Man 2011 was a fantastic year for me. I wish I could go back to that time even for once. 

[h1]The Story:[/h1]
Metro: Last Light just like Metro 2033 is based on the novels by Dmitry Glukhovsky. This one is based on the novel Metro 2034. The story yet again follows our favorite Russian friend, Artyom. Metro: Last Light takes place a year after the events of Metro 2033. With D6 being found and now becoming a HQ for the Spartan Rangers and the threat of the Dark One's being eliminated. Everyone would think that life in the Metro is perfect right? Of course, there are the occasional mutants but no dark ones so it must be safe? Well not really. With the discovery of D6, the tensions of the four major factions of the Metro have escalated. The Fourth Reich is planning an attack on D6 which they dubbed Operation El Dorado and they are also planning to finish off the Red Line on the frontlines. The Red Line, on the other hand, appears to have developed greatly, with a larger number of soldiers featuring equipment and training on par with other factions such as the Reich. They now have the largest army in the whole Metro thanks to the introduction of conscription, the Red Line also now have a high number of NBC suits, heavily armored suits, ballistic shields, flamethrowers, and other high-end weaponry that they will plan to use to dominate the Metro. War is inevitable thanks to the discovery of D6. Your story starts in D6 when your old pal Khan makes an unusual discovery. 

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
● Amazing narrative
● Introduction of new weapons [b](Saiga 12, Preved, Ashot.)[/b]
● Bigger focus on the human factions
● Good performance
● Beautiful soundtrack
● Great and memorable characters [b](Pavel, Fedor, Simon.)[/b]
● New mutants [b](Shrimps, Spiderbugs.)[/b]
● New weapon attachments
● Very immersive
● Very atmospheric
● Beautiful graphics
● Steam trading cards
● Steam Achievements
● Free DLC

[h1]Cons:[/h1]
● Some bugs and glitches
● Random game crashes [b](It can happen at any moment of the game and it's f**king annoying.)[/b]
● Stutters on some occasional levels
● Tower DLC [b](It is a complete s**tfest of a DLC that is poorly tested and designed. I have no idea why they brought it back, they should've let it die with the old version of Last Light.)[/b]

[h1]Conclusion:[/h1]
If you have played Metro 2033 and thoroughly enjoyed it or just really liked it in general. Then you will love the sequel. Sure it has some small performance issues here and there, but I don't blame the game. It's more or less issues to do with the so-called redux versions. But Metro: Last Light still remains a very good game, it's a sequel done right. What is even more shocking is that Metro: Last Light was made by developers in Ukraine, and that was in the middle of the civil war. They had to smuggle in the supplies for this game they were working on. They had pretty rough conditions but they still managed to pull off a fantastic sequel to my beloved game. They have my utmost respect for that. Metro Exodus will be 10x better and as a Metro fan. I know that already. So buy Metro: Last Light and continue the great story and adventure of our one and only favorite badass Russian friend Artyom.

[h1]Overall rating 1000/10[/h1]

Metro: Last Light is honestly one of the best story-driven games I've ever played. I absolutely loved every second of it. The game takes everything that made the first Metro great and somehow improves on it in almost every way.

The gameplay feels like a unique mix of Dying Light and Tomb Raider, combining intense combat, exploration, survival elements, and an incredibly immersive atmosphere. From the moment I started playing, I was completely hooked.

The story is absolutely fantastic and, in my opinion, even better than the first game's story. Metro 2033 was already amazing, but Last Light manages to continue the narrative in such a satisfying way that it completely pulled me in. I really love how the developers directly build upon the events of the first game and continue the journey instead of starting over with something completely different. If you're looking for a game with a genuinely incredible story, this is it.

The graphics are excellent, the sound design is phenomenal, and the atmosphere is simply unmatched. There is always this constant feeling of tension, with horror elements mixed into the experience perfectly. Exploring the dark tunnels of the Metro never stops being exciting or terrifying.

The weapons are awesome and offer plenty of customization options, allowing you to adapt your playstyle however you want. Every weapon feels powerful and satisfying to use.

The NPCs also feel more developed and believable than before. They have more personality, more depth, and make the world feel much more alive.

Honestly, I have nothing to complain about. The story, gameplay, graphics, sound, atmosphere, weapons, and characters all come together to create an unforgettable experience.

Metro: Last Light is an absolute must-play and one of the best sequels I've ever experienced.
